sourceBasis: Task audit: 12 rows, Operations / Admin, one role (Gisselle Jimenez)

departments.name: Operations & Task Orchestration
team: Team members assigned tasks in ClickUp and Slack
departments.summary: Detects overdue tasks, unacknowledged action items, and billing or data-hygiene exceptions across ClickUp, Slack, Gmail, and GHL, and routes each one to a named human for action.

departments.name: Member Portal & Community
departments.summary: Track office-hours attendance and publish reminder and recap content inside the GHL Communities portal, while every member contact stays with a person.

departments.name: Meetings & Knowledge Capture
departments.summary: Converts meeting transcripts into action items, archived assets and reviewed recaps so decisions made on a call reach ClickUp, the team and, after review, the client.

departments.name: Client Onboarding
departments.summary: Trigger onboarding from the signed-and-paid event, hand a human an editable checklist and welcome-email draft, and file inbound client assets into the client's Drive folder.

departments.name: Marketing & Content Engine
departments.summary: Converts client call recordings into reviewed marketing output: content ideas, reel scripts, carousels, email copy, and case studies.

departments.name: Client Communications
departments.summary: Draft, triage, and file client email in Gmail, holding client-facing replies behind a human review gate.

departments.name: Paid Media Reporting
departments.summary: Produce weekly Google Ads and Meta Ads performance reports for every client account from one scheduled run, delivered to Slack for review.

initiatives.title: Inbox Triage & Auto-Filing
initiatives.currentProcess: Gisselle works the inbox daily, filing emails Whitney has already read into the appropriate client folder, applying the starring system by hand, and clearing a larger backlog on Mondays from mail that came in over the weekend.
initiatives.outcome: Classifies incoming mail against the client, partner, newsletter, and tools labels, files read no-action threads, and proposes a star state for everything that still needs a human.

Auto-filing of read, no-action threads

stats.detail: Across 7 departments: 14 from the audited task rows, 6 from the Aug 26 call, 1 in build, 2 paid media reporting.

rules: Store no client credentials or sensitive business data beyond what the automation requires.
Keep Meta, Drive, and reporting access scoped to the automations that need them.
Meter LLM use per automation run.
Start with the four foundation automations before scaling model spend.
Set per-automation alerts for unusual usage.
Prefer scheduled batch runs over always-on generation where possible.
Keep a manual fallback so a failed automation does not lose data or block client delivery.
Deploy and test every automation in staging before production.
Deliver a functional MVP before adding every configuration option.
Collect Explore Media feedback after two to four weeks on each live automation.
Apply feedback in the following sprint.
Only release versions that provide immediate operational value.

reviewGates.reviewer: Whitney Hodges, with Gisselle Jimenez drafting and marking threads ready
reviewGates.rule: Generated replies and recaps stay in the Gmail drafts folder, marked ready for review. Whitney Hodges sends every AI-drafted client reply. Gisselle Jimenez's existing discretion on threads she writes herself — short acknowledgements, something a client has already approved, or when Whitney Hodges says so in Slack — is unchanged and does not extend to generated drafts.

reviewGates.reviewer: Gisselle Jimenez, with Whitney Hodges on the welcome email
reviewGates.rule: ON-01 presents an editable draft — rename tasks, change assignees and dates, remove rows — and a human batch-approves it; approval is terminal and nothing writes to ClickUp in this build. ON-02 checklist items and due dates are confirmed against the ClickUp onboarding template before assignment, and the welcome email leaves as a draft.

Filing and asset archival run without per-item approval. Gisselle Jimenez reviews an exceptions list of anything the workflow could not classify. No email thread is deleted, and vendor newsletters under the tools label are never auto-archived.

Action items, ClickUp tasks and the overdue digest go to Gisselle Jimenez before they post to Slack or get assigned. She confirms owner and due date on each; the chase sequence pauses on anything she holds.

reviewGates.reviewer: Gisselle Jimenez and Whitney Hodges, with the responsible team member on member follow-up
reviewGates.rule: These raise a flag and stop. MP-01 marks the 2-week and 4-week absence notches and the responsible team member sends the portal DM or the email. OP-03 flags overdue invoices and invalid emails to Gisselle Jimenez and Whitney Hodges. CC-03 lists waiting threads with no reply and Whitney Hodges decides which get a follow-up; any draft that produces goes through the client communications gate.

MP-02 posts from a template Gisselle Jimenez has approved, filling only session name, date and time.
